set timeout 240
  set cfg    $env(CC_RR_CFG)
  set bin    $env(CC_RR_BIN)
  set model  $env(CC_RR_MODEL)
  set effort $env(CC_RR_EFFORT)
  set sid    $env(CC_RR_SID)
  set thr    $env(CC_RR_THRESHOLD)
  set mcpdec $env(CC_RR_MCP_ARGS)
  set answered 0
  # The env prefix is a LIST so the suppression variable can be absent rather than empty. Passing
  # NAME= with no value is not the same thing: Rue() reads "" as NaN and falls back to the default
  # of 70 baked into the binary, which raises the dialog on every session older than 70 minutes —
  # i.e. "off" would look identical to "on" from here. One spawn line, appended to, so the two
  # paths cannot drift apart the way two spawn lines would.
  # NO APOSTROPHES ANYWHERE BELOW THIS LINE: the whole program is a single-quoted bash string, so
  # one apostrophe in a Tcl comment closes it and the rest of the file stops being expect at all.
  set envpfx [list DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER=1 CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=$cfg]
  if {$thr ne ""} { lappend envpfx CLAUDE_CODE_RESUME_THRESHOLD_MINUTES=$thr }
  # A LIST again, and for the second reason this file already gives: an absent decision must pass
  # NO argument, not an empty one, and appending the value as a single element keeps a path with a
  # space in it one argument rather than two.
  set mcplist [list]
  if {$mcpdec ne ""} { lappend mcplist $mcpdec }
  spawn -noecho env {*}$envpfx $bin --permission-mode auto --model $model --effort $effort {*}$mcplist --resume $sid
  # keep the claude UI responsive: propagate iTerm2 pane resizes (SIGWINCH) to the spawned pty.
  # interact does NOT forward window-size changes, so without this the Ink UI stays frozen at the
  # spawn-time width (verified 2026-07-05).
  trap {
    set rows [stty rows]
    set cols [stty columns]
    catch {stty rows $rows columns $cols < $spawn_out(slave,name)}
  } WINCH
  expect {
    # ── THE RESUME DIALOG. Two defects lived in the one line this replaces. ──
    #
    # WRONG OPTION. It answered with a bare CR, which takes whatever the cursor is resting on —
    # option 1, "Resume from summary". That runs /compact on the transcript: the session comes back
    # as a precis of itself, and (REFERENCE.md section 5) drops its session-scoped /goal Stop-hook,
    # which is why recovered sessions then sit idle. A crash recovery is supposed to return the
    # session. The operator wants option 2, "Resume full session as-is".
    #
    # WIDTH-DEPENDENT MATCH. "Resume from summary" is a 19-character literal and Ink hard-wraps to
    # the pane width, so on a pane narrowed by a recovery layout the phrase is split across rows and
    # the match never fires at all — the session then sits on an unanswered menu until the timeout,
    # which is how three transplants parked 20+ minutes.
    #
    # So the trigger is as-is: five characters, narrow enough that no usable pane can break it, and
    # present in exactly one place in the dialog — option 2 label. Not the title, and NOT the body
    # ("we recommend resuming from a summary"), which matters for the reason lr-fire-resume:178
    # documents: the body streams several seconds before Ink mounts the SelectInput and enables raw
    # mode, so anything triggered on it is answered into a terminal that is not listening yet.
    # Verbatim from the 2.1.220 bundle, in render order:
    #   [{value:"compact",  label:"Resume from summary (recommended)"},
    #    {value:"continue", label:"Resume full session as-is"},
    #    {value:"never",    label:"Do not ask me again"}]
    # RE-CHECK that list on any CC bump. Option 3 dismisses the dialog PERMANENTLY for the account,
    # so an extra Down here is a persistent preference change, not a mis-click — which is why the
    # move below is a clamp and exactly one step, never a loop.
    -re {as-is} {
      if {!$answered} {
        set answered 1
        # settle for raw mode, then move DETERMINISTICALLY. Up clamps at the first option, so three
        # of them cost nothing and leave the cursor at a KNOWN place whatever it did before; one
        # Down then lands on option 2.
        sleep 2
        send "\033\[A"; send "\033\[A"; send "\033\[A"
        sleep 1
        send "\033\[B"
        sleep 1
        send "\r"
      }
      exp_continue
    }
    -re {you created or one you trust|Quick safety check} { sleep 1; send "1"; send "\r"; exp_continue }
    -re {spent .* on the Anthropic API this session} { send "\r"; exp_continue }
    # fullscreen upsell: Down+CR selects "Not now" (option 2). RE-CHECK on any CC bump.
    -re {new fullscreen renderer|Try the new fullscreen} { sleep 1; send "\033\[B"; send "\r"; exp_continue }
    -re {shift.tab to cycle}  { }
    -re {auto mode on}        { }
    -re {\? for shortcuts}    { }
    timeout {}
    eof { exit }
  }
  # interact needs a controlling tty, so it is the one thing a headless harness cannot run. The
  # tests drive everything above this line — the real spawn, the real matcher, the real keystrokes.
  if {$env(CC_RR_NO_INTERACT) ne ""} {
    set timeout 20
    expect eof
    exit
  }
  interact
